findings.title: SPEC-877-D's claimed exit 0 for tests/intake-admission-e2e.mjs did not reproduce on independent re-run, on Windows, following the documented recipe exactly
findings.evidence: The fix report (wave4-lane07-fix.md, SPEC-877-D) states the root cause is stale `clara.wakes_outbox` rows re-becoming held wake tasks on every boot, and that settling those rows (held->cancelled) before running the leg on a disposable clone of clara_l07 produces 'INTAKE ADMISSION E2E: PASS (8 legs ...)' and exit 0, 'on Windows and again under WSL as runner'. I built two independent clones of the current clara_l07 (clara_878, clara_879), applied the documented settle exactly (clara.wakes_outbox held->cancelled, clara.agent_tasks non-terminal->cancelled), ran the WDK world bootstrap, and ran `node tests/intake-admission-e2e.mjs` on Windows against each. Both runs failed at the file's own closing `waitForQueueDrain` after the full 30000ms window: the first run's unbound-work dump names 8 freshly-created `clara.agent_tasks` rows of kind='wake', status='held' (not the pre-existing residue, which had already been cancelled) plus one `clara.document_processing_tasks` row stuck behind the 0051 §2 'no transport metadata in its sidecar' guard (`packages/runtime/lib/reconciler-documents.mjs:396-413`); the second run's dump names the same 8 fresh held wake tasks with no document-processing block. `clara.wake_intents` on clara_l07 has no 'pending' rows (all 7 are 'consumed'), so the 8 new held wake tasks are not re-derivations of stale intents — they are produced by the leg's own run and never clear inside the 30s window. This mechanism (wake-engine, queue-drain.mjs, drain.mjs) is entirely unchanged by this lane's diff (`git diff cd2925391...HEAD -- packages/runtime/tests/queue-drain.mjs packages/runtime/lib/drain.mjs` is empty), so this is not a regression from the lane's own commits, but it does mean the SPEC-877-D evidence table's specific, repeatable 'exit 0' claim is not something I could reproduce twice in the same conditions the report describes.
findings.required_fix: Before closing #877 on this claim, either (a) re-run the exact recipe once more and attach the actual terminal output/log (not just the summary line) so the orchestrator can see what differed from this recheck's two failing runs, or (b) if the exit-0 runs depended on local render/sandbox credentials (CLARA_RENDER_FLY_API_TOKEN/CLARA_RENDER_FLY_APP/CLARA_RENDER_FLY_MACHINE_ID/CLARA_RENDER_IMAGE_REF — both my runs logged 'render/sandbox dispatch UNWIRED ... falls back to the scheduled wake (delayed, not stranded)' repeatedly, which is a plausible source of wake tasks that do not clear inside 30s) or on WSL-only timing, say so explicitly in the report and in packages/runtime/README.md's new recipe section, so the next person following that recipe on a bare Windows checkout is not left assuming a plain settle-and-run reproduces the pass.

notes: All nine SPEC/F1 findings the fix report claims to have addressed (SPEC-1041-B, SPEC-1041-A, SPEC-1035-A, F1, SPEC-1033-A, SPEC-877-C, SPEC-877-A, SPEC-877-B, SPEC-877-D's code/comment portion) were independently re-read against source and, where they touch code the fix changed, re-run: all hold except the SPEC-877-D exit-0 EVIDENCE claim specifically (RECHECK-877-D-1 above). The four review notes the fix report left untouched (SPEC-1041-C, SPEC-1035-B, SPEC-1035-C, SPEC-1033-B) and F2 (standards note) needed no action and none was demanded by either review; unchanged, correctly.

Working tree left clean: no tracked file was edited, no commit was made. Scratch admin scripts used to query/settle/drop the two recheck clone databases (clara_878, clara_879) were created and removed within packages/db and are not present in the final `git status`.

Rig hygiene: two throwaway clone databases (clara_878, clara_879) were created from clara_l07, mutated (wake state settled, WDK schema bootstrapped) and dropped again via a direct DDL drop (tests/rig-cluster-reset.mjs's --drop-database refuses non-'*_ci'-shaped names). Cluster now reads exactly clara_l07, postgres — the same two it held before this recheck. CLARA_RIG_ALLOW_ROLE_SWEEP was never set; no role sweep was run.

Everything else measured in the fix report's Gates table that I independently re-ran (the db touched-file suite, the runtime touched-file suite, ready.test.mjs, typecheck, CI-mode lint, frozen-workflows, parts-parity, and the three touched-YAML files' syntax) reproduced the exact counts/results claimed, with nothing newly broken.
summary: Eight of the nine findings the fix round claims to have closed hold up on independent re-read and re-run: the code changes for SPEC-1041-B (gate-chain floor/skip-bound on frontier-leg steps 3c and 4, plus the awk-not-grep|head|awk pipefail fix), SPEC-1035-A (the step-9 paragraph in packages/runtime/README.md) and F1 (frontierViolationPhrase(v) as the single violation describer) match their commit messages exactly against source, and every db/runtime gate the fix report measured reproduces the same pass/fail/skip counts on a fresh run of this recheck (57/56/0/1 db, 63/41/0/22 runtime, 25/25/0/0 ready.test.mjs, typecheck and CI-mode lint both exit 0). SPEC-1041-A and SPEC-877-A/B/C are doc/comment-only and read as claimed. The one item that does NOT hold on re-verification is SPEC-877-D's central evidence claim: I followed the fix report's own documented recipe (settle clara.wakes_outbox and clara.agent_tasks on a disposable clone, bootstrap the WDK world, run tests/intake-admission-e2e.mjs) twice, independently, on Windows, and both runs timed out in waitForQueueDrain rather than exiting 0 — on newly-created held wake tasks the settle step does not touch (not stale residue; clara.wake_intents has none pending), and once also on a genuinely undispatchable document_processing_tasks row. The mechanism involved (wake-engine/queue-drain/drain.mjs) is unchanged by this lane's diff, so this is not a code regression the lane introduced, but it means the specific 'exit 0, Windows and WSL' evidence in the fix report is not independently reproducible as described, and the report and README should say what environment condition (credentials, WSL-only timing, or something else) the successful runs actually depended on before #877 is closed on that evidence.
